rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so this table pushes obfuscation intensity up while keeping guards against overhead and miscompiles: FLA gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain since AMGmk's large control-flow-heavy functions (hypre_CSRMatrixUnion, GenerateSeqLaplacian, the Matvec variants) are the primary reverse-engineering targets, but its RuntimeCost stays at 0.65 so the weight table biases flattening away from the hottest numeric loops (Matvec/relax inner kernels) whose features scream runtime cost; BCF and IBR sit just below FLA to add bogus-path and indirect-branch layering on medium-hot functions without compounding flat-out overhead on the same code; SUB is kept strong (0.70 security) since arithmetic substitution is cheap relative to its analysis-blocking value in this integer/pointer-heavy CSR code; SPLIT stays low-cost/low-gain as a diversity amplifier that also gives FLA more basic blocks to work with; ICALL and IGV round out coverage at moderate levels to obscure call targets and global state without inflating the binary. CorrectnessRisk weights are held uniformly high (0.65-0.75) because round 1's clean run came from that conservatism — the per-pass selectors should still decline passes on functions where risk features spike, preserving the correct execution we already verified while trading a modest amount of runtime headroom for substantially stronger protection.
